vision_features.image_context: Close-up photograph of a single broad leaf, viewed from the upper (adaxial) surface. The leaf is large, ovate with a pointed tip, and shows a prominent central midrib with branching secondary veins. Part of a second leaf and a green stem are visible in the background. The plant appears to be a broadleaf species, possibly a legume based on leaf shape and texture.
vision_features.abnormalities: 1. Small to medium circular/angular spots scattered primarily across the mid and lower-central portions of the leaf surface, concentrated between and along the secondary veins. Each spot has a dark reddish-brown to near-black center (approximately 1–4 mm in diameter), dry in appearance, with a surrounding pale yellow to yellow-green halo approximately 3–8 mm in diameter. The spots do not appear raised or sunken significantly from the leaf surface. 2. A cluster of larger, more coalesced dark spots is present on the left-center area of the leaf, where several individual marks appear to have merged, forming an irregular patch approximately 10–15 mm across with a deep reddish-purple to black coloration and a diffuse yellow-green margin. 3. The spots are distributed in a somewhat scattered but concentrated band running horizontally across the middle third of the leaf. Smaller, earlier-stage spots consist mostly of yellow halos with a tiny dark reddish-brown central point (pinpoint to 1 mm). 4. No surface structures (powder, thread-like growth, pustules) are clearly visible on the upper surface at this resolution.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or dusty coating is visible on either the upper leaf surface or within the marks. 2. No raised pustules or blister-like structures are visible on the upper surface. 3. No wilting, curling, or distortion of the leaf margin or blade is present. 4. No signs of physical tearing, insect feeding damage, or webbing are visible.
vision_features.summary: The leaf surface displays numerous small, discrete spots each consisting of a dark reddish-brown to near-black dry center surrounded by a pale yellow to yellow-green halo. The spots range from pinpoint size to approximately 4 mm in diameter, with one larger coalesced cluster on the left-center area of the leaf reaching about 15 mm across. The spots are concentrated in the middle portion of the leaf and are scattered between the secondary veins. The most striking feature is the strong contrast between the dark, dry central points and their bright yellow surrounding halos against the otherwise healthy green leaf tissue.

────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. ────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Leaf lesions with yellow halos vs. stem cankers/black specks in linear rows on stems
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into tattered dead areas; symptoms appear primarily on young leaves in the upper canopy.
Diaporthe: Sunken gray-brown stem cankers with reddish margins near nodes (stem canker form), or distinctive linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems (pod and stem blight form); may also show black zone lines inside lower stems.
Decision rule  : IF lesions are angular, on leaves, with a conspicuous yellow halo and tattered appearance, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF symptoms are on stems with sunken cankers at nodes OR linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems, THEN suspect Diaporthe (Disease B).
